security_spec.violation_condition: XiangShan RTL hardcodes mvip/mvien (or hip/hvip/hvien) CSR fields to read-only zero based on the removed Smaiae extension's constraints, but the CSR module now claims direct Smaia/Ssaia dependency per the updated spec — software relying on virtual interrupt injection via these CSRs (e.g., supervisor-level interrupt preemption or delegated interrupt handling) will silently fail because the hardware ignores writes to virtual interrupt pending/enable bits that the full AIA spec permits to be implemented as WARL-writable
security_spec.summary: Removal of Smaiae embedded subset and direct routing of ACLIC dependencies to full Smaia/Ssaia means virtual interrupt CSRs (mvip/mvien) must follow AIA WARL rules — hardcoding them to read-only zero (the old Smaiae behavior) causes silent virtual interrupt delivery failure, which is a hardware-level privilege escape where supervisor interrupts that should be injectable per spec are permanently masked

findings.finding: MvienBundle correctly implements AIA spec: SSIE (bit 1) and SEIE (bit 9) are RW per spec strong recommendation; local interrupt enable bits (14-63) are RW; LCOFIE (bit 13) and non-local non-HS bits (VSSIE, MSIE, STIE, VSTIE, MTIE, VSEIE, MEIE, SGEIE) remain RO via InterruptEnableBundle defaults, which is spec-correct. No Smaiae-related hardcoding to read-only zero exists.

spec_citations.excerpt: When supervisor mode is implemented, the minimal required implementation of mvien and mvip has all bits being read-only zeros except for mvip bits 1 and 9, and sometimes bit 5, each of which is an alias of an existing writable bit in mip.

findings.finding: MvipBundle correctly implements AIA spec: HS interrupt pending bits (SSIP, STIP, SEIP) are RW; local interrupt pending bits (14-63) are RW; LCOFIP (bit 13) is RO. The mvip module logic (lines 142-181) correctly implements alias vs independent register behavior based on mvien bits for SSIP, STIP (gated by menvcfg.STCE), and SEIP.

spec_citations.excerpt: When supervisor mode is implemented, the minimal required implementation of mvien and mvip has all bits being read-only zeros except for mvip bits 1 and 9, and sometimes bit 5, each of which is an alias of an existing writable bit in mip.

findings.finding: mvip alias logic correctly implements AIA spec: SSIP is independent writable when mvien.SSIE=1, alias of mip.SSIP otherwise (lines 146-149). STIP aliases mip.STIP when writable, read-only zero when menvcfg.STCE=1 (lines 154-157). SEIP alias/independent logic per mvien.SEIE (lines 162-166). Local interrupt writes forwarded from sip/vsip (lines 173-181).
findings.snippet:
reg.SSIP := Mux(wen && this.mvien.SSIE.asBool, wdata.SSIP, reg.SSIP)
regOut.SSIP := Mux(this.mvien.SSIE.asBool, reg.SSIP, this.mip.SSIP)
toMip.SSIP.valid := wen && !this.mvien.SSIE.asBool
toMip.SSIP.bits := wdata.SSIP

findings.finding: mip.SEIP correctly implements: when mvien.SEIE=0, mip.SEIP is alias of mvip.SEIP (writable); when mvien.SEIE=1, mip.SEIP is read-only zero. Read value correctly ORs mvip.SEIP with platform IRQ and AIA sources (line 282). References riscv-aia issue #64 for correctness rationale.
findings.snippet:
toMvip.SEIP.valid := wen && !this.mvien.SEIE
toMvip.SEIP.bits := wdata.SEIP
regOut.SEIP := Mux(!this.mvien.SEIE, this.mvip.SEIP.asUInt, 0.U)
rdataFields.SEIP := regOut.SEIP || platformIRP.SEIP || aiaToCSR.seip

findings.finding: HvienBundle correctly implements AIA spec: bits 12:0 are RO ("reserved and must be read-only zeros" per hypervisor spec), local interrupt enable bits 14-63 are RW, LCOFIE (bit 13) is RO. No Smaiae-related incorrect hardcoding.

HvipBundle correctly implements: VS interrupt pending bits (VSSIP, VSTIP, VSEIP) are RW; local interrupt pending bits 14-63 are RW; LCOFIP (bit 13) is RO. Writes accepted from mip, hip, and vsip correctly muxed (lines 116-129).

sie correctly implements mvien-based alias logic: when mideleg=1, sie is alias of mie; when mideleg=0 and mvien=1, sie uses its own register (usingReg). Hardwired bits (M-mode and VS-mode bits) are set to zero as required. sip module (line 102) similarly uses mvipIsAlias = ~mideleg & mvien for correct virtual interrupt routing.
findings.snippet:
val mieIsAlias = mideleg
val usingReg   = ~mideleg & mvien
regOut := (mieIsAlias & mie) | (usingReg & reg)

findings.finding: ssAiaHaddr list omits mvip/mvien, but this is correct: mvip/mvien are M-mode CSRs (addr 0x308/0x309, addr[9:8]=0b11). Non-M-mode access is already blocked by privilege-level check. The mstateen0.AIA bit controls non-M-mode access per smstateen spec, which is already forbidden for these M-mode CSRs. Adding them to the AIA check would be redundant.
findings.snippet:
private val ssAiaHaddr = Seq(CSRs.hvien.U, CSRs.hvictl.U, CSRs.hviprio1.U, CSRs.hviprio2.U)
private val ssAiaVSaddr = addr === CSRs.vstopi.U
private val ssAiaSaddr = addr === CSRs.stopi.U
private val csrIsAIA = ssAiaHaddr.map(_ === addr).reduce(_ || _) || ssAiaVSaddr || ssAiaSaddr
private val accessAIA_EX_II = csrIsAIA && !privState.isModeM && !mstateen0.AIA.asBool

spec_citations.excerpt: The AIA bit in mstateen0 controls access to all state introduced by the Ssaia extension and not controlled by either the CSRIND or the IMSIC bits.

findings.finding: LCOFIP and LCOFIE are RO (hardwired zero) in both MvienBundle and MvipBundle, as well as in HvienBundle and HvipBundle. This is correct since XiangShan does not implement the Sscofpmf extension (counter-overflow interrupts). No Sscofpmf references found in NewCSR directory.
findings.snippet:
this.LCOFIE.setRO().withReset(0.U)  // in MvienBundle
this.LCOFIP.setRO().withReset(0.U)  // in MvipBundle

spec_citations.excerpt: For implementations that support Smcdeleg, Sscofpmf, and Smaia, the local-counter-overflow interrupt (LCOFI) bit (bit 13) in each of CSRs mvip and mvien is implemented and writable.

findings.finding: MipBundle correctly implements: LCOFIP is RW with reset 0; HS bits (SSIP/STIP/SEIP) and VS bits (VSSIP/VSTIP/VSEIP) are RW; M-mode bits (MSIP/MTIP/MEIP) are RO as platform-level interrupts. This matches the AIA spec where some bits in mip are RO aliases of platform/mvip signals.
